                              - Code to replicate plots and analyses of: A record-breaking heatwave reduces breeding success and impairs growth in a wild bird population -
                                                Analysing and plotting temperature differeces during the heatwave year and the historical data
      
```{r}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

#Load data
```{r}
combined_temperature_data <- read_csv("combined_temperature_data.csv")
```

Compute relevant metrics
```{r}
summarise_period <- function(data, period_dates, label) {
  data %>%
    filter(date %in% period_dates) %>%
    summarise(
      period                  = label,
      n_days                  = n(),

      # Mean temperature values in each period
      mean_temp_2026          = mean(temp_2026, na.rm = TRUE),
      mean_temp_2023_2025     = mean(temp_hist, na.rm = TRUE),
      se_temp_2023_2025       = sqrt(sum(se_hist^2, na.rm = TRUE)) / n_days,
      mean_temp_cet           = mean(temp_cet,  na.rm = TRUE),
      se_temp_cet             = sqrt(sum(se_cet^2,  na.rm = TRUE)) / n_days,
      max_temp_2026           = max(temp_2026, na.rm = TRUE),

      # Differences between heatwave year and hitorical data
      mean_diff_vs_2023_2025  = mean(diff_vs_2023_2025, na.rm = TRUE),
      se_diff_vs_2023_2025    = sqrt(sum(diff_vs_2023_2025_se^2, na.rm = TRUE)) / n_days,

      mean_diff_vs_cet_degC   = mean(diff_vs_cet, na.rm = TRUE),
      se_diff_vs_cet_degC     = sqrt(sum(diff_vs_cet_se^2, na.rm = TRUE)) / n_days,

      mean_diff_vs_cet_SD     = mean(diff_vs_cet_sd, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
}

period_full  <- seq(as.Date("2026-05-22"), as.Date("2026-05-29"), by = "day")
period_peak  <- seq(as.Date("2026-05-25"), as.Date("2026-05-26"), by = "day")

results <- bind_rows(
  summarise_period(combined_temperature_data, period_full, "22–29 May 2026"),
  summarise_period(combined_temperature_data, period_peak, "25–26 May 2026")
)

results
```

Plot the temperature trends 
```{r}
hist_ribbon <- read_csv("hist_ribbon.csv")
mean_2023_2025 <- read_csv("mean_2023_2025.csv")
mean_2026 <- read_csv("mean_2026.csv")


trends_three_lines_2 <- ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = mean_2023_2025,
            aes(x = hour_common, y = mean_temp, colour = "2023-2025 mean"),
            linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(data = mean_2026,
            aes(x = hour_common, y = mean_temp, colour = "2026"),
            linewidth = 1) +
    geom_ribbon(data = hist_ribbon,
              aes(x = hour_common, ymin = hist_min, ymax = hist_max,
                  fill = "Historical mean ± range (1772-2025)"),
              alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(data = hist_ribbon,
            aes(x = hour_common, y = (hist_min + hist_max) / 2,
                colour = "Historical mean ± range (1772-2025)"),
            linewidth = 1, linetype = "solid") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(
    "2026"                                = "#E05C1A",   # darker orange for white bg
    "2023-2025 mean"                      = "#69AAA2",   # deeper blue for white bg
    "Historical mean ± range (1772-2025)" = "grey40"     # dark grey instead of white
  )) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Historical mean ± range (1772-2025)" = "grey60"     # visible ribbon on white bg
  )) +
  guides(
    colour = guide_legend(
      override.aes = list(
        linetype  = c("solid", "solid", "solid"),
        linewidth = c(1.5, 1.5, 1.5),
        fill      = c(NA, NA, "grey60")
      )
    ),
    fill = "none"
  ) +
  scale_x_datetime(date_breaks = "2 days", date_labels = "%b %d") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(4, 31),          # sets the axis range (min, max)
    breaks = seq(4, 31, by = 3) # controls where the tick marks/labels appear
  )+
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Temperature (°C)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 18) +
  theme(
    legend.position  = "bottom",
    axis.text.x      = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "grey85",linewidth = 0.25),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text        = element_text(colour = "grey20"),
    axis.title       = element_text(colour = "grey20"),
    legend.text      = element_text(colour = "grey20")
  )
  
trends_three_lines_2
```
